'''''Hypericum patulum''''', known as '''goldencup St. John's wort''' or '''yellow mosqueta''', is a species of flowering plant in ''[[Hypericum]]'' [[Hypericum sect. Ascyreia|sect. ''Ascyreia'']].

== Taxonomy ==
''Hypericum patulum'' was originally described by [[Carl Peter Thunberg]] in 1784. It was first published in [[Systema Vegetabilium]] later that year by [[Johan Andreas Murray]].<ref name="IPNI"/>

The species has a [[Sporophyte|sporophytic]] and [[Gametophyte|gametopythic]] chromosome count of 18 each.<ref name="Wlliams 1984"/><ref name="Sanger 1965"/>

=== Subordinate taxa ===
''Hypericum patulum'' has 5 accepted variants as subordinate taxa:<ref name="Tropicos"/>
* ''H. patulum'' var. ''attenuatum'' <small>Choisy 1824</small>
* ''H. patulum'' var. ''forrestii'' <small>Chitt. 1923</small>
* ''H. patulum'' var. ''henryi '' <small>Bean 1905</small>
* ''H. patulum'' var. ''hookerianum '' <small>(Wight & Arn.) Kuntze 1891</small>
* ''H. patulum ''var. ''uralum'' <small>(Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don) Koehne 1893</small>

=== Cultivars ===
''Hypericum patulum'' is cultivated as a garden plant under the name ''Hypericum'' 'Hidcote' or ''Hypericum'' x ''hidcoteense'' 'Hidcote'. It is grown for its large, bright flowers and its attractiveness to pollinators such as bees and small birds.<ref name="RHS"/>

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native only to the [[Guizhou]] and [[Sichuan]] provinces of [[China]], but it has been naturalized in [[Japan]], [[Taiwan]], and [[India]], as well as in [[Australia]] and [[South Africa]]. The species is also widely cultivated for garden use in temperate regions.<ref name="GRIN"/><ref name="POWO"/>

The species is found at elevations of {{Convert|1200-3600|m|ft|sp=us}}<ref name="EOL"/> in dry and open habitats, especially in thickets, on scrubby slopes, and on cliffs.<ref name="MySpecies"/>

== Description ==
Plants of the species are shrubs that grow from {{Convert|0.3-1.5|m|ft|1|sp=us}} tall. They grow in a bushy fashion, with spreading branches that are sometimes weakly frondose. The stems are 4-lined or 4-angled when the plant is young but later become 2-lined, and sometimes become terete. The leaves are thick and paper-like and are rather glaucous, with short laminar glands, streaks, and dots. Its inflorescence is 1–15-flowered that blossom from 1 or 2 nodes. The flowers are flat-topped, and sometimes have a short terminal internode and branches that come from the middle of the stem. The petals are a golden yellow color, without any tinge of red. The stamen fascicles, each with 50–70 stamens, grow to be up to 7–12 mm, and are about half as long as the petals. The seeds are dark brown and grow from 1–1.2 millimeters long.<ref name="eFloras"/>
